# insurancerating <img src="logo.png" align="right" width="120"/>

<!-- badges: start -->

[![CRAN Status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/insurancerating)](https://cran.r-project.org/package=insurancerating) [![Downloads](https://cranlogs.r-pkg.org/badges/insurancerating?color=blue)](https://cran.r-project.org/package=insurancerating)

<!-- badges: end -->

`insurancerating` provides actuarial building blocks for insurance pricing in
R. Use them alongside standard modelling functions such as `glm()` to analyse
portfolio experience, interpret fitted effects, turn them into implementable
tariffs and validate predictions. The package also supports risk-factor
structuring, large-loss treatment and preparation of large portfolios.

The building blocks can be used independently or combined to suit the
portfolio. The examples illustrate choices, not a prescribed methodology.

## Installation

Install the CRAN version, or install the development version from GitHub:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
install.packages("insurancerating")

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("MHaringa/insurancerating")
```

## Explore portfolio experience

`factor_analysis()` summarises observed experience and the exposure supporting
each level of a rating factor. These unadjusted portfolio patterns are useful
before modelling, but should not be interpreted as conditional tariff
relativities. Compare an apparent difference with the exposure and claim count
behind it.

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.alt = "Factor analysis plot showing claim frequency, average severity and risk premium by ZIP code."}
library(insurancerating)

portfolio <- as.data.frame(MTPL)
portfolio$zip <- factor(portfolio$zip)

zip_analysis <- factor_analysis(
  portfolio,
  risk_factors = "zip",
  claim_count = "nclaims",
  exposure = "exposure",
  claim_amount = "amount"
)

autoplot(
  zip_analysis,
  metrics = c("frequency", "average_severity", "risk_premium")
)
```

## From model to refined tariff

An age-band GLM estimates one relativity per band. Here we use age decades
where practical and pool ages 80 and above. A spline smooths the fitted
effects, which are then translated into new tariff bands.

```{r refinement-preview, fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 4.3, fig.alt = "Original GLM relativities, a dashed spline and new tariff bands. All three rise at the oldest ages."}
age_breaks <- c(18, 29, 39, 49, 59, 69, 79, 95)
portfolio$age_band <- cut(portfolio$age_policyholder, age_breaks,
                          include.lowest = TRUE)

frequency_model <- glm(
  nclaims ~ age_band + offset(log(exposure)),
  family = poisson(),
  data = portfolio
)

tariff_breaks <- c(18, 24, 30, 40, 55, 70, 79, 95)
proposal <- frequency_model |>
  prepare_refinement(data = portfolio) |>
  add_smoothing(
    "age_band", "age_policyholder",
    breaks = tariff_breaks, smoothing = "spline", k = 6, weights = "exposure"
  )

tariff <- refit(proposal, intercept_only = TRUE)
autoplot(proposal)
```

The blue steps are the original GLM estimates. The dashed curve is the
smoothing proposal; the orange steps are the resulting tariff bands.

In this sample, the fitted frequency rises from 9.1 to 12.3 claims per
100 policy-years between ages 70--79 and 80+. The oldest band contains
36 claims, so treat the rise as a feature of this example rather than a
general age effect.

`refit()` holds those band effects fixed and re-estimates the base claim rate,
so their relativities do not move again. See the
[refinement example](https://mharinga.github.io/insurancerating/articles/refinement-workflow.html#quick-start)
for how to inspect the fitted result.

## What does insurancerating help with?

| Pricing task | Main tools |
|---|---|
| Explore portfolio experience | `factor_analysis()`, `outlier_histogram()` |
| Structure continuous risk factors | `risk_factor_gam()`, `derive_tariff_segments()` |
| Interpret fitted model effects | `rating_table()`, `add_factor_experience()` |
| Refine tariff structures | `prepare_refinement()`, `add_smoothing()`, `add_restriction()`, `refit()` |
| Validate fit, calibration and risk ranking | `model_performance()`, `calibration_analysis()`, `discrimination_analysis()`, `validate_performance()` |
| Treat large losses | `assess_excess_threshold()`, `redistribute_excess_loss()` |
| Reduce portfolio data locally | `rating_grid()`, `merge_date_ranges()` |
| Reduce portfolios in a database | `rating_grid_db()`, `merge_date_ranges_db()` |

## Where should I start?

- [Getting Started](https://mharinga.github.io/insurancerating/articles/getting-started.html)
  Follow one portfolio through risk-factor analysis, modelling, technical risk
  premium, interpretation, validation and refinement.

- [Pricing workflow and package building blocks](https://mharinga.github.io/insurancerating/articles/pricing-workflow-building-blocks.html)
  See how the main actuarial pricing tasks and package components fit together.

- [Motor insurance case study](https://mharinga.github.io/insurancerating/articles/motor-pricing-case-study.html)
  Compare a fitted frequency model and candidate tariffs on a multi-year
  synthetic portfolio, including individual impact and a held-out year.

- [Refinement building blocks](https://mharinga.github.io/insurancerating/articles/refinement-workflow.html)
  Translate estimated model effects into an explicit, reviewable and
  implementable tariff structure.

- [Model validation](https://mharinga.github.io/insurancerating/articles/model-validation.html)
  Assess model fit, stability and tariff plausibility, compare observed with
  expected claims, and evaluate predictions on later periods. Start with the
  [quick start](https://mharinga.github.io/insurancerating/articles/model-validation.html#quick-start).

- [Large Portfolios](https://mharinga.github.io/insurancerating/articles/large-portfolios.html)
  Reduce production-sized portfolios with model-point aggregation and
  database-backed workflows.
